podcast.title: Early Band Formations
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, Matt Bellamy was the guitarist for drummer Dominic Howard's high school band, Carnage Mayhem, which subsequently became Gothic Plague. He later joined Dominic and another member in a band called Rocket Baby Dolls, which, at a teacher's suggestion, changed its name to Muse. "Matt Bellmi then became the guitarist for drummer Dominic Howard's band Carnage Mayhem, which then became known as Gothic Plague."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Guinness Record for Guitar Destruction
podcast.body: Matt Bellamy of Muse is recognized by the Guinness Book of World Records as the all-time champion guitar smasher, having destroyed 140 guitars during the band's 2004 tour in support of the "Absolution" album. "Matt Bellamy of Muse. When the band's 2004 tour wrapped up, and this is the one in support of the Absolution album, it turned out that he had totaled, destroyed, ruined, 140 guitars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: In-Ear Monitors for Stage Mobility
podcast.body: As the lead singer of Muse, Matt Bellamy is known for his extensive movement during live performances. His ability to "run around as much as he does" is facilitated by in-ear monitors, which provide him with a consistent and clear personal mix, independent of his location on stage. "met Bellamy couldn't possibly run around as much as he does without in-ear monitors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influenced by Jeff Buckley
podcast.body: The singer of Muse is noted as another prominent vocalist who has often referenced Jeff Buckley, indicating a significant influence on their vocal style and artistic approach. This highlights Buckley's lasting impact on contemporary music. "el cantante de míos que también ha hecho referencia a Jeff Buckley muy a menudo."

podcast.title: Proficiency on Piano and Guitar
podcast.body: Matt Bellamy, best known for his guitar work with the band Muse, is also recognized as a highly skilled piano player. He is specifically noted as being "no slouch at the piano," indicating significant proficiency on the instrument alongside his guitar talents. "Matt Bellamy of Muse, also known for his guitar work, but he's no slouch at the piano."

xref.body: His significant impact on guitar technique and technology in the late 1970s and early 1980s is used as a point of comparison for Matt Bellamy's influence in the 2000s. "What Eddie Van Halen was to the late 1970s and early 1980s, you could say that Matt is the equivalent to the 2000s."

xref.title: Connection to Muse's Matt Bellamy
xref.body: The rhythm guitarist in The Tornados was George Bellamy. Sixteen years later, George had a son named Matt, who in 1994 formed a band that became known as Muse. "16 years later, George had a son named Matt. And in 1994, Matt formed a band that became known as Meek's."
